clue.text: Girls with good spectacles

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
lasses are girls, chiefly in Scottish and northern English use

explanation.surface: Some girls are being admired for their fine eyewear.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for good goes in front of the girls, even though the clue names the girls first.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses and spectacles are both names for a pair of lenses worn to correct eyesight.

clue.text: Snag caught in strange light

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the other word
strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Something has been snagged in an odd glow.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a minor fault or hitch, the same as a snag.

clue.text: Calculator in a taxi returned by you and me

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returned means the taxi word goes back the way it came

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A calculator left in a taxi was handed back to the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame with sliding beads used to do arithmetic, an early calculator.

clue.text: Love article in knitted sweater

indicators.note: in places the article inside the other letters
knitted yarn is looped into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the definite article

explanation.surface: A knitted sweater as a love token.
explanation.definitionFit: Love and sweetheart are both affectionate terms of address for a beloved person.

clue.text: French philosopher lifted spicy fruits

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Albert Camus, French existentialist writer

explanation.surface: A French thinker pinched some spicy fruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reads as 'stole', but in a down answer it means turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub whose dried red berries are ground into a tangy spice used in Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Legacy of live pursuit

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a quest is a search or pursuit

explanation.surface: Someone's inheritance turns out to be a lifelong pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is property left to someone in a will, which is exactly what a legacy is.

clue.text: Prevent artist, copper and district attorney getting fish

parts.note: to bar is to prevent
RA is a Royal Academician
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
DA abbreviates district attorney

explanation.surface: An artist, a policeman and a prosecutor are stopped from catching fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman beside the attorney, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a long predatory sea fish with sharp teeth.

clue.text: Square vehicle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quadrangle, an enclosed courtyard
second meaning: a ... bike, a four-wheeled motorbike

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a boxy car; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word is both a college courtyard, a quadrangle, and an all-terrain four-wheeled bike.

clue.text: Former lover with abundant special specimens

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means plentiful
S is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: An ex has plenty of remarkable samples.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples and specimens are both individual items taken as representative of a type.

clue.text: Guess Walcott gets increase

parts.note: Theo Walcott, the England footballer
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: A footballer is guessing he will get a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form an idea without proof, much like making a guess.

clue.text: Statue of one magician

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a mage is a wizard or magician

explanation.surface: A statue has been put up depicting a single conjuror.
explanation.definitionFit: An image can be a carved likeness of a person or god, such as a statue.

clue.text: Doctor made alarm spread

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor's actions have caused panic to spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a noun at the start, but it is a verb meaning tamper; 'spread' is a noun, something you put on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve eaten on toast, an example of a spread.

clue.text: Piece of bread and a tin containing European crayfish, perhaps

indicators.note: containing says the tin holds the next item inside it

parts.note: a crust is a piece of bread
taken as written
a can is a tin
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A recipe step: bread and a tin holding European crayfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of bread' is one unit, not a selection signal; the European letter goes inside the tin, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayfish is a freshwater crustacean, so it is one example of the class; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Level recreation area removing back section

indicators.note: removing the back section means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a park is a public recreation area

explanation.surface: A park is being levelled by taking out its rear part.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is a level of equality, as in 'on a par with', or a standard norm.

clue.text: Trial never organised beside the point

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A court case that never got arranged is now moot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irrelevant has no bearing on the matter, which is the idiom 'beside the point'.

clue.text: Measure of liquid found in dive's nerve centre?

indicators.note: found in means one item sits inside the other

parts.note: headers are headlong dives; the apostrophe-s is read as a plural
a quart is a unit of liquid measure

explanation.surface: A seedy bar, a 'dive', where drink is measured is the hub of activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive' suggests a seedy bar, but here it is a headlong plunge, as in football; read the apostrophe-s as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Headquarters is the main office from which an organisation is directed, its nerve centre.

clue.text: Toiletry item old and young explorer found in pit

indicators.note: found in means these sit inside the next word

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or pit
O is the abbreviation for old
Dora the Explorer, the children's cartoon girl

explanation.surface: A toiletry is found down a pit with an old explorer and a young one.
explanation.walkthrough: Dora the Explorer is an American children's cartoon about a young girl who goes exploring.
explanation.definitionFit: A deodorant is a product applied to the body to mask odour, a typical toiletry.

clue.text: Lean on the French ship, exhausted

parts.note: to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does
les is French for the (plural)
S is an abbreviation for ship, as in SS

explanation.surface: A French ship leans over, worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lacking energy or enthusiasm, the state of someone exhausted.

clue.text: Bring about celebration

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to cause something
second meaning: a noun, a special event or party

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to throw a party; the verb and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to cause; as a noun it is a special event marked by festivities.

clue.text: Woven indoor carpet is included

indicators.note: weaving interlaces strands into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woven rug for indoors comes as part of the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incorporated has been taken in as part of a whole, which is to say included.

clue.text: Column with a line related to mail

parts.note: a post is an upright column
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A newspaper column with one line about the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Postal is the adjective for anything to do with the post or mail service.

clue.text: Stake fish for shop

parts.note: to stake is to bet
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone wagers on fish to buy at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is a verb: to inform on someone to the police, British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, which betrays them.

clue.text: Heads of traditional eatery assembled meal

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the initial letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Bosses of an old-fashioned restaurant have gathered for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' is a link word here, meaning the letters put together make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain, not just the drink.

clue.text: Phone has place to rest in caravan

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile phone
home is where you rest

explanation.surface: A phone has found somewhere to sit in a touring caravan.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile home is a large caravan used as a dwelling, so the two describe the same kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Awkward writer upset during sex

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An awkward author is upset during intimacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like distress, but in a down answer it turns the writer upside down; 'it' as a coy word for sex is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill, which matches awkward.

clue.text: Piece of vital importance is drooping

indicators.note: a piece of something is a part of it, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Something of vital importance is sagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means lacking firmness and hanging loosely, so it describes something drooping.

clue.text: Remove cream covering minute appetiser's top

indicators.note: covering means the cream wraps around what follows

parts.note: the elite are the cream of society
MIN is the abbreviation for minute

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of appetiser

explanation.surface: A cook is told to take off cream covering the tip of a tiny starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like 'tiny', but it is the unit of time; 'cream' means the best people, not dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to get rid of it entirely, so it is a strong synonym of remove.

clue.text: Player is rubbish and about to be rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back the way it came, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
ca. (circa) means about

explanation.surface: A performer is dismissed as rubbish and is about to be turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be' reads as 'soon to be', but 'about' gives CA and 'to be rejected' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs a part on stage, so an actor.

clue.text: Son with cap going back to play area

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
with means plus, and

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a tip is a cap or end piece, as on a walking stick

explanation.surface: A boy wearing a cap heads back to the playground.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpit is a shallow area of sand where small children play.

clue.text: Quite high during play

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another

parts.note: to toy is to play
tall means high

explanation.surface: Someone got quite high while watching a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' suggests intoxication and 'play' a stage show, but they are tall and a verb meaning to trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite in its strong sense means completely, as in 'quite right', which is what totally means.
